children: JGBs rise in the early Tokyo session, tracking overnight price gains in U.S. Treasurys. Both JGBs and Treasurys tend to move in tandem. Dovish comments by Fed's Waller sent yields lower, ING's Benjamin Schroeder says in a research report. "All eyes are on the [U.S. nonfarm] payrolls' data after recent Fed commentary has raised the stakes for a hike while making it also more dependent on the final jobs and inflation data ahead of the [Fed's] meeting," the senior rates strategist adds. The yield on the No. 382 10-year JGB is down 4 bps at 2.920%. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
